chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal said: He narrated to me Ali ibn Ya'qub, from Abu al-Baghdadi, from al-Hasan ibn Isma'il ibn Salih al-Saymarri, who said: He narrated to me al-Hasan ibn Rashid, who said: He narrated to me Hammad ibn Isa, who said: One of our companions narrated it to me, mentioning it from the righteous servant, Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him).

He said: 'Khums is due from five things: from the spoils of war, from diving (for pearls), from treasures, from minerals, and from coral.' And in the narration of Yunus: 'and amber,' I found this word alone in some of his books: 'amber,' and I did not hear it.

One-fifth is taken from each of these categories, and it is assigned to whom Allah has assigned it to. Four-fifths are distributed among those who fought for it and had authority over it. The one-fifth portion is divided among them into six shares: a share for Allah, a share for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), a share for the near relatives, a share for the orphans, a share for the poor, and a share for the wayfarers.

Thus, the share of Allah and the share of the Messenger belong to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). The share of Allah and the share of the Messenger belong to the Imam (Guardian of Affairs) after the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) by inheritance. Therefore, he has three shares: two by inheritance, and one share allocated to him by Allah. Thus, he possesses the entire half of the Khums. The remaining half of the Khums is distributed among his family: a share for their orphans, a share for their poor, and a share for their wayfarers.

It is distributed among them according to their sufficiency and capacity, to the extent they need to be self-sufficient for their year. If there is a surplus that they do not need, it belongs to the Imam. If it is insufficient or falls short of their need for self-sufficiency, it is upon the Imam to spend from his own resources to cover the shortfall. Thus, it becomes incumbent upon him to provide for them because he owns the surplus that remains from them.

Allah designated this Khums specifically for them, distinct from the poor of the people and their wayfarers, as a substitute for them from the charity of the people. This is to honor them from Allah due to their kinship with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and to grant them dignity away from the dust of the people's charity. Thus, He gave them a specific portion from Himself that makes them self-sufficient so as not to place them in a position of humiliation and poverty.

There is no harm in some of them giving charity to others. These are the ones for whom Allah designated the Khums: they are the relatives of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) whom Allah mentioned: 'And warn your closest kindred' (1). They are the Banu Abd al-Muttalib, both males and females among them. No one from the houses of Quraysh or from the Arabs is included in them, nor are their freed slaves (Mawali) included in this Khums, neither from their side nor from the side of the Prophet.

The charity of the people is permissible for their freed slaves, as they are equal to the people. And whoever has a mother from Banu Hashim and a father from the rest of Quraysh, charity is permissible for him, but he has no share in the Khums, because Allah the Exalted says: 'Call them by [the names of] their fathers' (2).

The Imam has the right to take the best of the wealth from these assets: the flowing, fine currency, the fine mount, or the garment, or the goods, of whatever he loves or desires. This is for him before the distribution and before the payment of Khums. He may use this wealth to cover all expenses that befall him before giving to those whose hearts are to be reconciled and other categories of expenses that befall him.

If anything remains after that, he pays the Khums from it and distributes it among his family, and distributes the remainder among those who have authority over it. If nothing remains after covering the expenses, then they have nothing. Those who fought have no share in the land or what they conquered, except what the army contained. The Bedouins have no share in the distribution, even if they fought with the Imam.

Because the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) made peace with the Bedouins by leaving them in their lands and not requiring them to migrate, on the condition that if an enemy attacked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), he would summon them to fight with him. They have no share in the spoils, and his practice continues to apply to them and others.

The land that was taken by force with cavalry and infantry is held in trust, left in the hands of whoever cultivates and revitalizes it and manages it, according to the peace treaty the Imam makes with them, based on their capacity for the land tax: half, or one-third, or two-thirds, and according to what is beneficial for them and does not harm them.

When it is taken over and initiated, one-tenth (Ushr) is extracted from all that is watered by rain or by natural flow, and half of the tenth from that which is watered by manual or animal labor. The Imam takes it and directs it in the manner Allah directed, across eight shares: for the poor, the needy, the workers upon it, those whose hearts are to be reconciled, for freeing slaves, for debtors, in the way of Allah, and for the wayfarer.

Eight shares, which he distributes among them in their locations according to what they need to be self-sufficient for their year, without hardship or stinginess. If something remains from that, it is returned to the Imam. If something is lacking and they are not satisfied with it, it is upon the Imam to provide for them from his own resources to the extent of their full sufficiency until they are self-sufficient.

Afterward, what remains of the tenth is taken and distributed between the Imam and his partners, who are the workers and tenants of the land. Their portions are given to them according to what they agreed upon. He takes the remainder, which becomes the provisions for his assistants, in accordance with the religion of Allah and the interest of what befalls him in strengthening Islam and the religion in the face of jihad and other matters of public interest.

He does not take a little or a lot for himself from that. After Khums, he has the Anfal. Anfal is every barren land whose people have perished, and every land that was not conquered by marching with cavalry and infantry, but rather a treaty was made with them and they gave it with their own hands without fighting. He owns the peaks of mountains, the bottoms of valleys, the thickets, and every dead land that has no owner.

He owns the surplus of kings from what was in their hands not by usurpation, because all usurped property is returned. He is the heir of one who has no heir, and upon him falls every one who has no means of support.

And the Jurist (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah does not leave any of the categories of wealth without having distributed it, and He gives every person with a right their specific right, of the specific and the general, the poor and the needy, and every type of people.' He said: 'If justice were established among the people, they would be self-sufficient.' Then he said: 'Indeed, justice is sweeter than honey, and only one who excels in justice can be just.'

He said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) distributed the charity of the settled people among the settled people, and did not distribute it equally among them across the eight shares so that each share recipient gets an equal portion. Rather, he distributed it according to who was present from the eight categories, and according to what would suffice each category for their year. There was nothing fixed or specified or predetermined in this; he did it according to what he saw and what was present, until he covered the need of every group among them.' If there was a surplus from this beyond the needs of the poor of the wealthy, he transferred it to others.

And the Anfal belong to the Imam. Every land conquered in the time of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) until the end of eternity, whether conquered by the call of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) from the unjust or the just, because the covenant of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) with the first and the last is one covenant, because the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The Muslims are brothers, their bloods are mutually equal, and the lowest among them runs with the covenant of the highest among them.'

There is no Zakat in the wealth of Khums, because Allah made the sustenance of the poor of the people from the wealth of the people across eight categories, and no one from them remained without provision. He made half of the Khums for the poor of the Prophet's relatives (peace be upon him and his family), thereby making them self-sufficient from the charity of the people, the charity of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and the Imam. Thus, no poor person from the people remained, and no poor person from the Prophet's relatives remained without being self-sufficient. There is no poor person, and likewise, there was no Zakat on the wealth of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and the Imam, because no needy poor person remained. However, expenses befall them from many aspects, and they have from those aspects as much as they have upon them.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَيْتِ: The People of the House (Prophet's family)

ai.seo_question: What are the five sources of Khums and how is the one-fifth portion distributed between the Imam and the Prophet's family?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elaborates on the Shia jurisprudence of Khums, distinguishing it from Zakat by assigning half to the Imam as the inheritor of the Prophet's spiritual and material authority, thereby elevating the Ahl al-Bayt above the general populace. It further details the Imam's prerogative to select the finest assets (Safwa) for state needs before distribution and clarifies the status of Anfal and conquered lands, emphasizing the Imam's role in ensuring the financial independence of the Prophet's clan.
